title: Pretend family budget and price list
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y4 lesson 7 (Pretend family budget and price list (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 7: Family expenses. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.title: Sort into: Essential / Nice to have
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Essential, Nice to have.
blocks.answer: Essential: Electricity; Food shopping; Water bill; Internet for school. Nice to have: Takeaway pizza; New video game

panels.title: Saving energy saves money
points: Lights off when leaving a room

blocks.h: My family budget: £100 for the week

blocks.answers: Essentials first: food £60, electricity £15, water £8, internet £7 = £90. £10 left: for example sadaqah £5 and savings £5. No takeaway, game or day out this week (they would go over £100).

keywords.def: a request to pay for a service, like electricity
something a family must pay for

questions.q: Why is internet essential for our family at TGA?
questions.a: Our lessons are online on Teams.

questions.q: Name two ways you can save energy at home.
questions.a: Lights off, shorter showers, close the fridge.

questions.q: Core: Pretend family budget: £100 for the week. Choose spending from the price list so essentials come first (pupil PDF).
questions.a: Essentials (food, bills) chosen first and total no more than £100.

questions.q: Extend: Write a thank-you note to a grown-up for something they pay for.
Stretch: Explain why bills must be paid before treats.
questions.a: Without paying bills, the family could lose essentials like electricity or water.
B) The water bill. Water is needed for life and hygiene; the others are wants.

questions.q: A bill is... A) a toy B) a request to pay for a service C) a coin
questions.a: B) a request to pay for a service
options: A request to pay for a service

questions.q: Big question: who pays for the light at home, and how?
questions.a: Grown-ups, by paying the electricity bill.
